text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government is considering reintroducing fee-paying game hunting on an experimental basis.
- President Daniel arap Moi says the government is distributing relief food to famine-stricken people without discrimination.
- The Electoral Commission views as nonesense fears in some western nations that the general elections will be marred by violence.
- A man who killed his father in a crime of passion walks free from a Mombasa court.
- Normal operations resume at Kisumu airport a day after it was closed by fire.
- The Kenya Revenue Authority rehabilitates two speedboats to combat drug trafficking and smuggling along Kenya's coast.
- U.N. secretary-general calls for U.N. member states to nominate more women to serve as special representatives.
- A housewife arrested after a robbery issues a notice to sue the attorney-general for damages.
- The chairman of the Kenya National Examination Council says the body did not "doctor" results to favour certain regions. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
